title: Honcho Administrator's Guide
subtitle: Step-by-step setup and everyday tasks for admins.

blocks.text: Honcho is the system Black Pilots of America (BPA) uses to run its membership. This guide is for the people who run it: Chapter, Member, Student, Content, Event, Financial and System Admins, and staff. Everything every member does (logging in, your own profile and card, rosters, the directory, finding documents) is in the **Honcho Member Guide**.
Honcho can be set up with different words for different organizations. In BPA's system a person is a **Member** and a local group is a **Chapter**, so that's what this guide says.
Your Role Decides What You See
Admin roles add menus and pages. Use the chapters that match your roles.

rows: Members chosen to run a chapter
Your chapter's members, posts, events, documents, exports, and your chapter's own AI and Coffee Report
All members, statuses, bulk changes, master spreadsheet
Members who manage the home page and website
Page sections, pictures, Sunshine, Bulletin Board, Marquee, Careers
Members who manage the events calendar
Every event on the calendar (Chapter Admins add their own chapter's)
Members and staff given library rights
Add, review and approve documents on the kanban board
The Treasurer, and anyone else they choose
Financial Settings: the current membership year, grace period, dues payment year, new-member dues
System Settings, Security Groups, member permissions, chapters, the audit log, and National's AI and Coffee Report
Staff and members on project teams (add-on)
Employees using the separate staff login

blocks.text: Roles are given on a member's record (Roles & Permissions) by a Member Admin or System Admin, or on the Security Groups screen. Someone sees new menus the next time they log in.

Admins reach their pages through **EMS** on the member home's side menu (the name is set on System Settings > Organization). It opens the admin side menu, with a section per role: Member Admin, Chapter Admin, Website, PMS, System Admin and Reports. Click a section to open its pages.

items: **Expand/Hide** at the top shrinks the menu to icons to give the page more room; click the arrows again to open it.
**Member Home** goes back to the member home page.
Pages have a **Close** button that returns to where you came from.

blocks.text: This Guide in Honcho

Click **Help** (side menu of the home page, top bar of profile pages, or **System Admin > Help & Guides**) to read this guide, the Member Guide and, for System Admins, the Developer's Guide, with a search box. Admin screens such as the Coffee Report settings have a **Help** or **?** button that opens the matching section.
If you're a Chapter Admin, the side menu has a **Chapter Admin** section, and the side menu's **EMS** item shows **Chapter Administration**. Everything here is limited to your own chapter.

rows: See and manage your chapter's members
Post illnesses and passings, sticky notes and job postings for all members or just your chapter, and approve your chapter members' sticky notes (see Chapter Posts)

Your chapter's documents in the Document Library (Chapter 5): add and edit them, move them on the kanban board, approve, hide or delete them, and manage comments. You can only change your own chapter's documents, and anything you add is saved to your chapter.
Download your chapter's members as a spreadsheet

When the AI module is switched on: your chapter's own daily email for its Chapter Admins: your chapter's membership numbers, events, posts and documents, plus weather, news and YouTube sections you choose, by email and optionally to a Telegram chat. Preview, Send a test (to you or to the whole list), Telegram test, and a list of what was sent

When the AI module is switched on: your chapter's own AI provider account, if it wants one (API key, model, monthly limit, Test connection). Your chapter pays that provider directly. Without one, your chapter uses National's AI or none, as National decides

blocks.text: Working With the Member List
Every member list works the same way. Each row has buttons at the right:

rows: Opens the member's profile for editing; click **Save Changes** when done
Removes the member from the active lists. This can be undone
Shown on deleted members: brings the member back
Shown on deleted members: removes the member and all their records for good. This cannot be undone

blocks.text: Use the search box above the list to find a member, and click a column heading to sort.
Bulk Actions
To change many members at once, tick the box on each row (or **Select** at the top to tick them all), choose an action from the **Bulk Actions** list below the table and click **Submit**.

rows: Marks the ticked members as members for the current year
Creates a login account for each ticked member who doesn't have one
Deletes the ticked members (can be undone one at a time with Undelete Record)

blocks.text: **Lock**, **Unlock**, **Approve User Acct**, **Approve CCMPS** and **Archive** also appear in the list but don't do anything yet.
Locking a Member

To stop a member logging in without deleting them, open them with **Update Record**, tick **Locked** in **Roles & Permissions** and save (System Admins only). When they try to log in they see "Your account has been locked. Please contact your Chapter Administrator." Untick **Locked** to let them back in.
Marking a Member Deceased
Open the member with **Update Record**, go to **Admin Notes**, tick **Deceased** and click **Save Changes**. When you save:

items: They can no longer log in, on the website or the phone app.
Every admin role the member had (System, Member, Chapter, Student, Content or Event Admin) is taken away, and they're removed from all Security Groups, including access to the Document Library.
They no longer appear on the chapter roster, the national directory, the treasurer's spreadsheet or the member counts.
Their record isn't deleted. You can still find it in the member list.
An email address isn't needed to save the record.

blocks.text: Unticking Deceased lets the member log in again, but doesn't give their roles back. If it was a mistake, give the member their roles again.
Adding a Member

Click the button to add a member above the list, fill in their details and save. To let them log in, either tick them and use the **User Acct** bulk action, or create the account from their record. They'll be asked to choose a new password the first time they log in.

Open **Sunshine**, **Bulletin Board** or **Careers** from the Chapter Admin menu. Each list shows the posts for your chapter, the posts you made for all members, and the posts your chapter's members made, with who posted each one. Use **Add** to post; the form works like the Content Admins' one (Chapter 4).

items: **Chapter:** posts start on **All Members**, so everyone sees them. Choose your chapter to show a post to your chapter's members only.
**Public website:** only Content Admins and System Admins can put a post on the public website. Ask one of them if a post should go there.

**Approving sticky notes:** any member can post a sticky note on the Bulletin Board, and it goes up straight away. If one shouldn't be there, change its **Approval** on the list (or in the form) to **Pending** or **Disapproved** and it comes off the board. Set it back to **Approved** to show it again. If the member changes a disapproved note, it comes back to you as Pending.
**Pictures:** you can choose a photo from the picture library for Sunshine and Careers posts. Content Admins add pictures to the library.
The Marquee is managed by the Content Admins.

blocks.text: **Chapter Events:** add and change your chapter's events on the events calendar from **Chapter Events** in the Chapter Admin menu (or the Events tile on the Admin page). Every member sees them on the calendar, marked with your chapter's name; tick **Public** to also show one on the public website. See Chapter 4, Events Calendar.
Member Admins manage membership across every chapter. The side menu has a **Member Admin** section, and the **Reports** section has the national roster and the master spreadsheet.

rows: Every member in every chapter. The number shows how many
The treasurer's roster of current members
Download all members as a spreadsheet

blocks.text: On the home page, the Admin tile also shows member counts by status: **Current**, **Past Due** and **Current Student**.
Working With the Member List
Every member list works the same way. Each row has buttons at the right:

rows: Opens the member's profile for editing; click **Save Changes** when done
Removes the member from the active lists. This can be undone
Shown on deleted members: brings the member back
Shown on deleted members: removes the member and all their records for good. This cannot be undone

Locking a Member

To stop a member logging in without deleting them, open them with **Update Record**, tick **Locked** in **Roles & Permissions** and save (System Admins only). When they try to log in they see "Your account has been locked. Please contact your Chapter Administrator." Untick **Locked** to let them back in.
Marking a Member Deceased
Open the member with **Update Record**, go to **Admin Notes**, tick **Deceased** and click **Save Changes**. When you save:

items: They can no longer log in, on the website or the phone app.
Every admin role the member had (System, Member, Chapter, Student, Content or Event Admin) is taken away, and they're removed from all Security Groups, including access to the Document Library.
They no longer appear on the chapter roster, the national directory, the treasurer's spreadsheet or the member counts.
Their record isn't deleted. You can still find it in the member list.

Statuses and the Current Year

A member's status (Current, Past Due, Pending, Expired) depends on their dues and the current membership year. At the start of a new year, use the **Current Year** bulk action on members who have paid. The current year itself and the grace period are set by a Financial Admin or System Admin (Financial Settings, Chapter 6).
To make someone a **lifetime member**, enter **2099** as their Current Year and save. Lifetime members are always Current, whatever the dues year.
Membership Cards

The **Card** button on a member's record shows their digital membership card. If they've lost their phone, **Cancel and issue a new card** stops the old QR code working at once. Chapter Admins can do this for their own chapter's members.
Giving Someone an Admin Role

Open the member with **Update Record**, go to **Roles & Permissions**, tick the roles they should have (for example Chapter Admin or Content Admin) and save. They see the new menus the next time they log in. System, Member, Chapter, Student, Content, Event and Financial Admin are kept in Security Groups, so the change also shows there. System Admins can also set everyone's roles from one list: **System Admin > Member Permissions** (Chapter 6).
Only give admin roles to people who need them. A Member Admin can see and change every member's details.

Content Admins (and System Admins) decide what the member home page and the public website show. Open **Website** in the side menu, or the Website tiles on the Admin page. Staff with the Content Admins Security Group see **Website** in the staff menu and use the same pages.

rows: Every section of the page, top to bottom: the picture slider, feature boxes, team, timeline, quotes, prices, contact details, and the Sunshine, Bulletin Board, Calendar, Marquee, Careers and member-numbers sections. Show or hide each one on the member home and on the public website, drag sections into a new order, and change headings
The pieces inside a section, such as the slides in the slider or the people in Team
Upload pictures once, then choose them for any slide or item
Illnesses, recoveries and passings: a name, the news, more details, a photo
Short notes shown as coloured sticky notes
One-line announcements that scroll across the page
Job postings. Each has its own page with the full description and an Apply button
The events calendar (Event Admins and System Admins: every event; Chapter Admins: their own chapter's events, under **Chapter Events** in the Chapter Admin menu)

blocks.text: What you enter shows on the lower part of the member home page, below the member tiles, in the order of the Page Sections list. A menu bar across the top of that part has a link for each section that has a menu label; clicking one scrolls down to it. A section that is switched off, or has nothing in it yet, doesn't show at all.

**The public website** uses the same sections, for anyone, without logging in. It shows only the sections whose **Public website** box is ticked, the Sunshine, Bulletin Board, Marquee and Careers posts ticked **Also on the public website**, and the events ticked **Public**. Member numbers never show there. Its menu has a **Member Login** button. Your system administrator decides whether the website is the site's front page; until then it can be viewed at the address ending in `welcome/website`.
The old Notices and Activities pages are gone: put announcements in the Marquee or on the Bulletin Board, and activities on the events calendar.

The Calendar section of the member home shows every chapter's events: national events in green, your own chapter's in blue and other chapters' in grey. Members can switch between **Month**, **Week** and **List**, and click an event to see its details and its button (for example **Register**). On a phone the calendar opens as a list.

items: **Who adds events:** Event Admins and System Admins add and change any event, national or for any chapter (**Website → Events**). Chapter Admins add and change their own chapter's events (**Chapter Admin → Chapter Events**, or the Events tile on the Admin page); their events are always saved to their chapter.

**Adding one:** click **Add an Event**. Give it a title and a start date; the start time, end date and end time are optional. Tick **All day** for an event without times. Add a location, a short description (shown in the details), a full description, a picture and a link with a button label if you like.
**Public:** tick it to also show the event on the public website's calendar, once the public site is built.
The list shows upcoming events; **Show past events** lists the ones that are over. **Delete** asks first and can't be undone.

**Show or hide:** tick or untick a section's **Member home** or **Public website** box. It saves straight away and a message at the top confirms it. Some sections, such as the member numbers, are for the member home only.
**Order:** drag a row by its handle (the three lines on the left) to a new place. The new order saves when you let go.
**Edit:** change the section's **heading**, an optional **subtitle**, and its **menu label**: the link in the page's top menu that scrolls down to the section. Leave the label blank for no link.
**Items:** sections you fill yourself have an **Items** button. Sections such as Sunshine or Careers get their content from their own pages instead.

blocks.text: The item form only shows the boxes that section uses, with labels that say what each is for (for example **Headline** and **Button link** for a slide, or **Name**, **Role** and **Photo** for a team member).

items: **Picture:** click **Choose a Picture** and pick one from the library. Upload new pictures on the Pictures page first. **No Picture** removes it.
**Icon:** a Font Awesome name such as `fa-plane`; a preview shows next to the box.
**Links** start with `https://`, `mailto:` or `tel:`, or `/` for a page on this site, or `#` for a section of the page.
**Shown:** untick to hide an item without deleting it. You can also tick or untick it on the Items list.
Drag items on the list to change their order. **Delete** asks first and can't be undone.

blocks.text: Each has a list (open it from the **Website** menu, or **Posts** on the Page Sections list) and an **Add** button. The form only asks for what that kind of post uses.

items: **Chapter:** leave it on **All Members**, or choose a chapter to show the post to that chapter's members only.

**Who else posts:** Chapter Admins post Sunshine, Bulletin Board and Careers items for all members or their own chapter (not the public website), and any member can post sticky notes on the Bulletin Board. The list's **Posted by** column shows who posted each one.

**Approval (Bulletin Board):** members' sticky notes go up straight away. Change a note's **Approval** to **Pending** or **Disapproved** to take it off the board, or back to **Approved** to show it again. A member's Chapter Admin can do the same.

**Show from / until:** both optional. A post appears on its start date and disappears after its end date by itself; blank means now and no end. The list's **Today** column says whether each post is showing, waiting to start, or ended.
**Shown:** untick to take a post down at once without deleting it. **Also on the public website** lets it appear there once the public site is built and its section is switched on for it.
New posts go to the top of the list; drag rows to change the order.
**Careers:** the short description shows in the list; the full description, employer and location, picture, closing date and **Apply** button show on the job's own page.
Click **Choose Files**, pick one or more JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP pictures (up to 10 MB each), then **Upload**. Very wide pictures are made smaller automatically so the page loads quickly.
Give each picture a short **description** of what it shows. Screen readers read it aloud to people who can't see the picture. It saves when you click out of the box.
Each picture shows how many times it's used. A picture can only be deleted when nothing uses it.

blocks.text: Pictures for the Slider
The slider on the member home and the public website is always **470 pixels tall**; its width follows the screen, so the picture is cropped to fit:
**Best size: 1920 x 640 pixels** (3 : 1), a JPEG under about 400 KB. Uploads wider than 1920 pixels are made 1920 wide automatically, so a larger picture gains nothing.

items: **Keep people and key details in the middle**, roughly the middle 60% of the width: the sides are cut off on narrower screens.
**Leave the left third fairly plain.** The slide's headline, text and button sit over it.
**Give heads room at the top.** The slider keeps the upper part of a picture, but a tall picture still loses some of its top and bottom.
**Avoid portrait and square pictures.** A 4 : 3 photo (for example 1024 x 768) is cropped heavily and looks soft stretched across a wide screen.

blocks.text: Finding, opening and downloading documents is the same for everyone: see the Document Library chapter of the Member Guide. Admins can also add documents and move them through the kanban board.
If your role allows it, click the button to add a document:

items: Choose whether this is a **record only** (no file, for example a note about a paper document) or **I will upload a file**.
Fill in the title, subject, descriptions and author.
Set the three labels (Organization, Category, Type), the access level and the priority.
Choose the file to upload, if there is one, and save.

blocks.text: If you upload a file with the same name as an existing one, the old file is kept as a backup rather than overwritten.
The kanban board shows documents moving from first draft to approval, one column per stage:

rows: An idea or rough draft. This column can be hidden
Ready for someone to work on
Approved and published. This column can be hidden

blocks.text: Each card has buttons to move it to another stage, open it, or comment on it. When an approved document no longer needs to be on the board, mark it **Done** to take it off.
Comments, Holds and Rejections

items: Add a **comment** to a document to give feedback; comments can be closed when dealt with.
A document can be marked **on hold** or **blocked**, with a reason shown on the card.
An approver can **reject** a document with a reason, or **approve** it, which clears any hold, block or rejection.

blocks.text: System Admins look after how Honcho is set up. These pages are under **System Admin** in the side menu.

rows: Every member's admin roles in one list (System, Member, Chapter, Student, Content, Event and Financial Admin). Click a box to give or remove a role

How the system is set up for your organization, in tabs: Financial, Organization, Wording, Look, Features & Policy and Document Library. See the next section. Only on installs without the staff portal (see below)
The sizes and colors offered in everyone's Display Size choices

When the AI module is switched on: a short daily email for National's admins with membership numbers, upcoming events, Sunshine and Bulletin Board posts, documents waiting for approval, and weather, news and YouTube sections you choose. Pick the days, time, recipients and tone, and optionally a Telegram chat to send it to as well (make a bot with @BotFather, paste its token, message the bot, then use **Find chat ID**); **Preview** shows today's report without sending, **Send a test** emails it to you or to everyone on the list, and **Sent** lists every report sent with the facts it was written from. With an AI connection the AI writes it up; without one the plain facts are sent

When the AI module is switched on: National's AI provider account (API key, model, on/off, monthly limit), a **Test connection** button, which chapters have their own, and **Usage** (requests and estimated cost by month). The key is stored encrypted and never shown again. A Claude or ChatGPT *subscription* can't be entered here; it takes an API key from the provider's console
A record of who did what and when: logins, changes, approvals and deletions. Only on installs without the staff portal (see below)
Groups of people and the functions each group may use. Only on installs without the staff portal (see below)
The "who can see it" choices for posts
Technical documentation for whoever maintains Honcho
Download every member as a spreadsheet

blocks.text: **Where System Settings, the Auditlog and Security Groups live.** When the Honcho staff portal is installed (as it is for BPA), these three pages are in the staff portal's **System Admin** menu, for staff system admins only, and they don't appear in the member menu. On a members-only install they're in the member **System Admin** menu, for members with the System Admin role; an installation can have a dedicated account for this that isn't a person (BPA's is **portaladmin**). Staff accounts always sign in at the staff login, not the member portal. Projects is part of the staff portal, so it isn't in the member menu.
Member Permissions

Lists members with a checkbox for each admin role. It opens showing only members who hold a role; click **Show all members** to give someone a role for the first time. Clicking a box saves straight away, shows a confirmation at the top and is recorded in the Auditlog. The member sees the change the next time they log in. Each box is a membership of a Security Group (Member System Admins, Member Admins, Chapter Admins, Student Admins), so the same change shows on the Security Groups page. If a member also gets a role from another group, the box can't be cleared here; the message says so.
You can't remove your own System Admin role, and there must always be at least one System Admin.
Changes to System Settings take effect for everyone straight away. Note the old value before changing one. Every change is recorded in the Auditlog with its old and new value.
Security Groups

A group is a named set of people, such as "PM Admins", together with the functions they may use. Click **New group** to create one, then use its **Privileges** button to tick its functions (one panel per module, with **Select all**) and its **Members** button to add people. Anyone with a login can be added; someone with both a member and a staff login appears twice. A person gets everything any of their groups allows, and a change works on their next click.
**Effective access** shows one person's groups and every function they end up with. **Deactivate** switches a group off without losing its settings. Every change is recorded in the Auditlog.
The **Modules** panel on the same page switches an add-on, such as Projects, on or off for everyone. When Projects is off, its pages and its menu item disappear.

Security Groups are new (October 2026). The modules move over to them one at a time, starting with Projects, which already uses them: whoever is in **PM Admins** or **PM Users** can open Projects, and adding someone to a project team gives them PM User access. Until a module has moved, its own permission settings still decide who can do what.
Using the Audit Log

Each entry shows the date and time (UTC), the person, the action and the record it touched. Use the search box to find all changes to one member or one document. The eye button opens one entry; the trash button deletes it (the deletion is itself logged).

**System Admin > System Settings** has one tab per kind of setting. Change the values on a tab and click **Save Changes**. Each setting has a line underneath saying what it does. If a value isn't allowed (for example a web address that doesn't start with https://), nothing is saved and the message at the top says what to fix.

rows: Current membership year, grace period, dues payment year, new member dues proration. See Financial Settings below
The organization's name and short name, the system name, the headings on the member and staff login pages, the public website address, the support phone number, Facebook, X and YouTube pages
What the system calls a member, a chapter and a staff member (singular and plural), the name of the Website menu, and what people are asked for after their password
Show or hide some fields of the member record (Department, Reports To and Lead Source so far). A hidden field disappears from the profile and the edit form; anything already stored in it is kept
The color scheme, the logo and header logo, and the extra button in the member home's top menu (for example a registration link)

Whether the site's front address shows the public website, whether members may post Bulletin Board sticky notes, the minimum password length, and whether new members must change their password the first time they log in
Document Library labels: the organization and tag names, the Kanban column headings, which columns show, and when the editing page opens

blocks.text: Color Scheme and Logos

On the **Look** tab, each color scheme is a card showing its six colors. Click a card and save, and every screen changes to those colors. **Classic** is the colors the site has always had. **Custom** lets you choose the six colors yourself: click a color box on the Custom card to open a color picker.

The six colors, left to right: **Primary** (site name, headings, member names), **Accent** (record box headers), **Highlight** (icons), **Label** (form labels, Back buttons), **Value** (the information beside labels) and **Menu** (the side menu).

For a new logo, first upload the picture under **Website > Pictures** (about 100 x 82 pixels looks best). Then choose it as **Logo** on the Look tab; a preview shows under the list. **Default logo** puts the original back.
Try a new scheme, look around a few screens, and switch back to Classic if you don't like it. Some older screens have colors of their own and don't follow the scheme yet.
Financial Settings
Financial Admins see only this tab. They reach it from **Financial Settings** in the Admin menu (members) or the side menu (staff). System Admins find it as the first tab of System Settings.

rows: The year in force. Members last renewed for an earlier year are Past Due or Expired
On: members behind on their dues show as **Past Due**. Off: they show as **Expired**
The only year members can pay dues for. Paying for more than one year goes through the Treasurer
The share of full dues a new member pays: 1.0 = full dues, 0.75 = 25% off, 0 = free

blocks.text: Changing the **current membership year** or the **grace period** changes members' statuses, so Honcho asks first. A page lists the changes and how many members will be re-checked; click **Save and re-check** to go ahead or **Cancel** to change nothing. When it's done, the message at the top says how many members' status changed.
Lifetime members (year 2099) always stay Current. To make someone a Financial Admin, tick **Financial Admin** on their member record, or in Member Permissions.

chapters.title: AI and the Daily Coffee Report

blocks.text: The **Daily Coffee Report** is a short morning email for admins: membership numbers, upcoming events, Sunshine and Bulletin Board posts, documents waiting for approval, and any weather, news and YouTube sections you choose. It can also go to a Telegram chat.

Honcho collects every fact itself. If you connect an AI, the AI turns those facts into a friendly, easy-to-read report; it is told to use only the facts it is given and to keep every number exactly. Without AI, or if the AI is unavailable that day, the plain facts are sent instead, so the report always goes out.

rows: National's AI connection and National's Coffee Report
National's report, if National sends it to admins
Their chapter's own AI connection (optional) and their chapter's Coffee Report

blocks.text: The AI module must be switched on first: **System Admin > Security Groups > Modules**, switch on **AI assistant (Honcho AI)**. Until then the AI and Coffee Report pages aren't in the menu.
Skip this step to send plain reports. To have the AI write them:

items: Sign in at **console.anthropic.com** with the account that will pay for the AI (or create one). Add a payment method.
In the Console, set a **monthly spend limit** for the account. This is your safety net.
Open **API keys** and create a key (name it, for example, "Honcho"). Copy it; it is shown only once.
In Honcho open **EMS > System Admin > AI Connections** (Chapter Admins: **EMS > Chapter Admin > Chapter AI**) and click **Set up** (or **Edit**).
Paste the key, choose a model (Claude Opus 5.5 is the default; Sonnet and Haiku cost less), set a **monthly limit** in dollars, leave Connection **On**, and click **Save**.
Click **Test connection**. "Connected: the AI answered" means it works.

blocks.text: A Claude or ChatGPT **subscription** (Pro, Max, Plus, Team) can't be used here. The providers allow those logins only in their own apps. Honcho needs an **API key**, which is billed by use.

items: The key is stored encrypted and never shown again; the screen shows only its last 4 characters.
When this month's estimated cost reaches your limit, the AI pauses until next month and reports go out plain.
**Remove key** (click twice) deletes the key and switches the connection off.
**Chapters without their own connection** use National's, or get no AI, depending on **System Settings > Features & Policy > Chapters without their own AI**.
**Usage** (on the AI Connections page) shows requests and estimated cost by month, National and each chapter.

blocks.text: Open **EMS > System Admin > Coffee Report** (Chapter Admins: **EMS > Chapter Admin > Coffee Report**) and click **Set up** or **Settings**.

rows: **Off** while you set it up; **On** when you want it sent every day
The time, your time zone, and the days of the week

Tick to send it to the scope's admins (National: System and Member Admins; a chapter: its Chapter Admins); the page names them. **Also send it to these addresses** always receive it, ticked or not: one per line. Each address gets one copy, even if it is also an admin's
How the AI should write, for example "Friendly and brief, for volunteer leaders reading on a phone". It never changes the facts
Tick the sections you want. The number boxes set their order (1 first). Fill in each section's options, then **Save**

blocks.text: The Sections

rows: Current members, past due, renewal rate; new members in the last 7 days
Approved calendar events (a chapter sees its own and National's)
Posts showing today on the member home
Document Library items in Pending Approval (a chapter: its own)
Locations, one per line, e.g. "Chicago, IL"
Recent headlines for each search topic, duplicates removed

Reports are emailed through Brevo, from an address Brevo has verified. This is done once, by whoever looks after the server:

items: In Brevo, open **Settings > Senders, Domains & Dedicated IPs > Senders** and add the address reports should come from (ideally one at the organization's own domain). Brevo emails a confirmation link to it; click it.
In the server's **.env** file set **MAIL_FROM_EMAIL** to that address and **MAIL_FROM_NAME** to the name people should see, for example "BPA Coffee Report".

blocks.text: On a test server (WHATENV=dev) every report goes only to the developer's address, never to real admins, so testing is safe.
The report can also go to a Telegram chat: one person, or a group with the admins in it. Email and Telegram are sent separately, so if one fails the other still arrives.

items: In Telegram, open **@BotFather**, send **/newbot**, choose a name and a username ending in "bot". BotFather replies with a **token** like 123456789:ABC....
For a group: add the new bot to your admins' group. For yourself: open the bot and press **Start**. Then post any message (in the group or to the bot).
In the report's settings, tick **Send to Telegram too**, paste the **bot token**, and click **Save**.
Click **Find chat ID**. Honcho lists the chats that have messaged the bot; copy the number (groups start with -) into **Chat ID** and **Save** again.
Click **Telegram test**. The report should arrive in the chat.

blocks.text: Long reports arrive as two or three messages. The token is stored encrypted; tick **Remove the saved bot token** and save to delete it. iMessage isn't available: it only works from an Apple computer, not a web server.

items: **Preview** builds today's report and shows it on the page. Nothing is sent. Use it while choosing sections.
**Send a test** emails it **To me** (your own address), or **To everyone on the "Sent to" list** as a dry run of the real email. If your account has no email address, only the list choice is offered.
**Telegram test** sends it to the Telegram chat.
When you're happy, set **Report** to **On** and **Save**. From the next scheduled time it goes out on the days you ticked, once a day.

blocks.text: The Sent List

**Sent** (on the Coffee Report page) lists every report sent: when, whether the AI wrote it, how many emails went out, whether Telegram worked, and any notes. **View** shows the report and, underneath, exactly what each section collected, so you can check the facts.

Employees use a separate staff login for the Honcho back office, not the member portal. After logging in they see a dashboard and a side menu with these sections: **Dashboard**, **DMS** (the Document Library), **PMS** (Projects), **CMS**, **Website CMS**, **People**, **Reports**, **System Configuration** and **Security**. Staff system admins also get **System Admin**, with **System Settings**, the **Auditlog** and **Security Groups** (described in Chapter 6).
The menu also links to the lists that other screens choose from: **Address Types**, **Bulk Actions** and **Post Scopes**. Changing an entry in one of these lists changes the choices everyone sees.
Staff with access to member records can switch to the member pages and use **Back to honcho** in the side menu to return.
A detailed staff guide will follow as the staff portal is updated.
